'''Frederick Terrell Jones''' (born March 11, 1979) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon Ducks]] and was the winner of the [[NBA Slam Dunk Contest]] at the [[2004 NBA All-Star Game]].

==Early career==
Born in [[Malvern, Arkansas]], Fred Jones moved to [[Portland, Oregon]], in middle school and became the Oregon High School Player of the Year in both his Junior and Senior years for [[Sam Barlow High School]] in [[Gresham, Oregon|Gresham]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Keizur |first=Christopher |date=2022-07-14 |title=Barlow's Fred Jones inducted into Oregon Sports Hall of Fame |url=https://www.theoutlookonline.com/sports/barlows-fred-jones-inducted-into-oregon-sports-hall-of-fame/article_d8357a8d-e76b-5b53-987d-0f89483b463b.html |access-date=2025-05-02 |website=TheOutlookOnline.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Martini |first=Pete |title=Former Ducks star Freddie Jones back in Eugene working on his next hoops career |url=https://www.statesmanjournal.com/story/sports/2016/02/15/former-ducks-star-freddie-jones-back-eugene-working-his-next-hoops-career/80394070/ |access-date=2025-05-02 |website=Statesman Journal |language=en-US}}</ref> a suburb of Portland. He then went on to play four seasons at the [[University of Oregon]], where, during his senior year, he led the Ducks to the [[Elite Eight]], with the help of [[Luke Ridnour]] and [[Luke Jackson (basketball, born 1981)|Luke Jackson]]. While widely considered to be an underachiever during his first three years at Oregon, Jones jumped onto the national radar screen as a senior, becoming a candidate for [[Pac-10]] Player of the Year and averaging 18.6 points per game.

== Professional career==

=== NBA ===
Jones was the 14th pick in the [[2002 NBA draft]] by the [[Indiana Pacers]]. He was drafted by [[Isiah Thomas]]. He played sparingly as a rookie, averaging only 1.2 points per game in 19 appearances while playing behind [[Reggie Miller]]. That scoring average increased to nearly 5 points per game in his second year while appearing in 81 games. He more than doubled his averages during the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05]] season (to 10.6 ppg), partly due to teammate and [[small forward]] [[Ron Artest]] being suspended for the season for his involvement in [[Pacers–Pistons brawl|The Malice at The Palace]] incident. In his first start after the incident, Jones scored a career-high 31 points against the [[Orlando Magic]], establishing himself as one of the team's primary scoring weapons.

In 2004, he won the [[NBA Slam Dunk Contest]], beating out two-time champion [[Jason Richardson]],<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--not stated--> |date= February 15, 2004|title=Jones wins dunk contest with a miss |url=https://www.deseret.com/2004/2/15/19812444/jones-wins-dunk-contest-with-a-miss/ |work= [[Deseret News]]|location=[[Los Angeles]] |access-date=March 25, 2024}}</ref> but did not compete in the contest again.

On November 23, 2004, against the [[Boston Celtics]], Jones recorded his first [[Double (basketball)#Double-double|double double]], with 16 points and a career-high 10 rebounds.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/jonesfr01/gamelog/2005/|title=Fred Jones 2004-05 Game Log|website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref> His three-pointer against the [[New Jersey Nets]] on March 22, 2005, earned Internet fame when a [[Ball State University]] student newscaster described it in his recap and followed with the phrase [[Boom goes the dynamite|"Boom goes the dynamite."]]

In the 2006 off-season, the [[Toronto Raptors]] signed Jones.<ref>[http://dwb.sacbee.com/24hour/sports/absketball/nba/15/story/3337953p-12291736c.htmlFred Jones joins Raptors]{{dead link|date=October 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}, July 26, 2006</ref> On February 22, 2007, the Raptors traded Jones to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for guard [[Juan Dixon]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/fred-211975-1218.html|title=BLAZERS: Portland Acquires G/F Fred Jones from Toronto- Send G Juan Dixon to Raptors<!-- Bot generated title -->|website=[[NBA.com]] }}</ref>

Jones, along with [[Zach Randolph]] and [[Dan Dickau]], was traded to the [[New York Knicks]] on June 28, 2007, for [[Channing Frye]] and [[Steve Francis]]. The trade reunited Jones with New York Knicks head coach Isiah Thomas, the man who drafted him. The Knicks did not re-sign him after the year.

On December 28, 2008, Jones signed with the Los Angeles Clippers as a free agent.<ref>{{cite web |title=Clippers Sign Guard Fred Jones |url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/fjones_081228.html |work=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2008-12-28}}</ref> He was waived on January 5, 2009,<ref>{{cite web |title=Clippers Waive Paul David and Fred Jones |url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/davis_jones_waived_090105.html |work=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2009-01-08}}</ref> however three days later he was again signed by the Clippers to a 10-day contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=Clippers Sign Fred Jones to 10-Day Contract |url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/fjones_090108.html |work=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2009-01-08}}</ref> On January 28, 2009, Jones received news that the Clippers would re-sign him for the rest of the season,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dailynews.com/ci_11578162?source=rss |title=SHELBURNE: Clippers guard Jones living Everyman's dreams - and fears - LA Daily News |website=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |access-date=2009-01-29 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110621234844/http://www.dailynews.com/ci_11578162?source=rss |archive-date=2011-06-21 }}</ref> which they did the following day.<ref name="Clippers Sign">{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/fjones_090129.html|title=Clippers Sign Fred Jones for the Remainder of the Season|website=[[NBA.com]] }}</ref>

Jones' final NBA game was on April 15, 2009, in an 85–126 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] where he recorded eight points and five assists.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fred Jones 2008-09 Stats per Game - NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/1718/fred-jones |access-date=2024-02-20 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref>

=== Italy ===
In August 2009 Jones signed with Italian team [[Pallacanestro Biella]].<ref>{{cite web |title=BIELLA lands Fred Jones |url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/ulebcup/home/news/transactions-2009/eurocup-2009-10/i/57784/3695/biella-lands-fred-jones |work=[[ULEB Eurocup]] |access-date=2009-08-20 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130122103351/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/ulebcup/home/news/transactions-2009/eurocup-2009-10/i/57784/3695/biella-lands-fred-jones |archive-date=2013-01-22 }}</ref>

===China===
On November 3, 2010, it was announced that Fred Jones had signed a contract to play for the [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.niubball.com/2010/11/fred-jones-signs-contract-with-guangdong-southern-tigers/ |title=Archived copy |access-date=2010-11-03 |archive-date=2021-05-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210504135736/http://niubball.com/2010/11/fred-jones-signs-contract-with-guangdong-southern-tigers/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was waived in January 2011.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cbachina.163.com/11/0114/23/6QD6IQ9000052UUC.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110118231848/http://cbachina.163.com/11/0114/23/6QD6IQ9000052UUC.html|url-status=dead|title=广东裁掉扣篮王新援哈德森火速上位次轮登场|archivedate=January 18, 2011}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
Jones returned to Oregon to complete his degree and was an undergraduate assistant coach for the Ducks in 2015–16.<ref>{{cite web|first1=Pete|last1=Martini|title=Former Ducks star Freddie Jones back in Eugene working on his next hoops career|url=https://www.statesmanjournal.com/story/sports/2016/02/15/former-ducks-star-freddie-jones-back-eugene-working-his-next-hoops-career/80394070|date=February 15, 2016|website=statesmanjournal.com|access-date=February 15, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first1=Drew|last1=Ruiz|title=FRED JONES TALKS DUNK CONTEST AND JORDAN PES|url=https://www.slamonline.com/nba/fred-jones-dunk-contest-jordan-pes|date=February 17, 2017|website=slamonline.com|access-date=February 17, 2017}}</ref>
